title: Microplastics in freshwater environments across the high altitude region of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.
abstract: Microplastics are increasingly recognized as pervasive contaminants in remote mountain freshwater ecosystems, yet evidence from high-altitude regions remains limited. This study investigated microplastics occurrence and characteristics in surface water, sediments, and fish from the Braldu-Shigar-Skardu freshwater system in Gilgit-Baltistan, northern Pakistan. Samples were collected from remote headwaters, tributaries, main river channels, and the Satpara Lake-Dam system. Fish originated from wild populations, farming facilities, and local markets to provide a broader assessment of microplastic exposure. Matrix-specific extraction protocols were applied, followed by stereomicroscope sorting and polymer identification by µFT-IR spectroscopy. Microplastics were detected in nearly all sites and matrices, with concentrations ranging from 1 to 17 MPs L-1 in water, 55-537 MPs kg-1 in sediments, and 1-11 MPs individual-1 in fish gastrointestinal tracts. Notably, highest frequency of microplastics occurrence was measured in farmed individuals (78%-83%), suggesting that aquaculture-related practices may represent an additional source of microplastics. Wild fish showed the lowest occurrence (25%), whereas those obtained from local markets revealed intermediate values (62%), indicating variable exposure across different pathways. Surface waters were dominated by small fragments and polypropylene, indicative of recent inputs and origin from fragmentation. Sediments showed a broader size distribution, and greater polymer diversity, consistent with their role as long-term sinks. The highest polymer diversity was highlighted in fish, indicating multiple exposure pathways. Spatial patterns did not show a geographical downstream increase, but rather a patchy distribution shaped by local anthropogenic input, hydrological connectivity, and depositional dynamics. Glacier-fed rivers primarily act as transport corridors, whereas low-energy environments such as Satpara Lake function as sinks promoting microplastics accumulation. Overall, the study provides the first integrated multi-compartment baseline for microplastics in Gilgit-Baltistan and supports future monitoring and management actions for these high altitude critical freshwater resources.

title: Microplastic contamination in Ramsar wetlands: a systematic review of global sources, ecological impacts, and policy implications.
mesh: Wetlands; Environmental Monitoring; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Microplastics; Environmental Policy; Geologic Sediments; Ecosystem
abstract: Ramsar wetlands, globally recognized for their ecological, hydrological, and socio-economic significance, are increasingly threatened by microplastic (MP) contamination. Despite mounting evidence of MPs in freshwater and coastal environments, no global synthesis has focused on MP contamination in Ramsar-designated wetlands. This study presents the first systematic global review of MP contamination in Ramsar wetlands by compiling peer-reviewed studies (April 2012-May 2025). This review addresses MP sources, transport pathways, contamination levels in surface water, sediment, and biota especially in threatened species, ecosystem impacts, and mitigation efforts. Key findings from quartile analysis and descriptive statistics reveal that MPs are ubiquitous across Ramsar wetland compartments, with spatial patterns showing higher contamination in Asia, North and South America, and lower levels in Europe and Australia. Certain countries' Ramsar wetlands consistently emerged as hotspots across all three environmental compartments, surface water, sediments, and biota, including Ecuador, China, India, and Ghana. Temporal trends indicate rising MP loads over the past decade, and seasonal peaks linked to runoff in some regions. Polyethylene and polypropylene were the most common polymers (> 80%), with fibres and fragments as the predominant morphotypes. Sediments generally harboured the highest MP concentrations, while biota exhibited variable uptake. These results underscore an urgent need for standardized monitoring methods and more geographically balanced research, especially in under-studied regions such as Africa and South America, to enable robust global comparisons. We recommend prioritizing plastic source reduction, enhancing international collaboration, and integrating MP pollution control into wetland conservation policies to safeguard the ecological integrity of Ramsar wetlands.

title: Photoinduced weathering of plastics and implications for spectral inclusion into matching database for laser direct infrared spectroscopy identification.
abstract: Microplastics are a ubiquitous environmental contaminant that can be found virtually every habitat and water source around the world. Therefore, there is great interest in developing efficient and reliable methodologies for the identification and enumeration of microplastics from environmental media. Laser direct infrared spectroscopy (LDIR) utilizes the fingerprint region of infrared (IR) spectra to make identification of plastics and other materials during analysis. However, only pristine spectra of plastics are currently used in the identification process. It has been well documented that the IR spectra of plastics changes considerably upon photochemical weathering, bringing into question whether databases may lead to misidentification of certain polymer types. To test if weathering influences identification of microplastics by LDIR, nine different plastics were irradiated to simulate weathering from 3 to 13 years in the sun. The physical and chemical changes of the plastic were measured by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) respectively. The weathered polymers were analyzed by LDIR-transflectance spectroscopy and resulting spectra were loaded into the LDIR matching database. This updated database was used to analyze samples from a local wastewater treatment plant with and without the inclusion of weathered spectra. This manuscript shows the inclusion of weathered transflectance spectra into the LDIR matching database can increase polymer identifications by 9.6 - 10.2% in wastewater samples on average. It also reveals that not all polymers are increased in identification uniformly, as PC and PA show the most sizeable increased spectral matches. However, most polymers tested were able to show increased medium and high-quality matches of weathered polymers using this approach.

title: Microplastics in freshwater aquaculture: Evidence of sediment-fish transfer and associated ecological risks in Bangladesh.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in aquaculture systems in Bangladesh threaten ecosystem health and food safety. This study examined MPs in surface sediments and farmed fish from 25 aquaculture ponds in Trishal Upazila, Mymensingh. Most sites were moderately to highly polluted, with a pollution load index (PLI) ranging from 1.0 to 4.5, while mean sediment MPs concentrations were 11.04 ± 3.75 particles kg-1. For fish, a total of 90 MPs were detected, with a mean abundance of 0.60 ± 1.16 MPs fish-1. Demersal fish (52%) demonstrated the greatest ingestion rates, followed by benthopelagic (35%) and pelagic species (13%). The major polymers detected were PE and PP, showing ubiquitous plastic origins in aquaculture and household activities. Frequency of occurrence (FO%) ranging from 16% to 40% revealed uneven fish species MPs ingestion rate. Fulton's condition factor (K: 0.35-2.27) varied among species, with lower values observed in Catla catla and Pangasius pangasius, which also showed relatively higher MPs ingestion. Higher bioconcentration (BCF) values in Cirrhinus cirrhosus, Cyprinus carpio and Pangasius pangasius indicating MPs magnification through the food chain. Overall, the widespread ingestion of MP by cultured fish highlights their potential ecological impacts within Bangladesh's aquaculture systems and underscores the urgent need for targeted monitoring and sustainable management strategies to mitigate MP contamination.

title: A versatile Bacillus esterase reveals a carboxylesterase blueprint for PET intermediate degradation.
mesh: Bacillus; Polyethylene Terephthalates; Carboxylesterase; Hydrogen-Ion Concentration; Substrate Specificity; Carboxylic Ester Hydrolases; Temperature; Kinetics; Biodegradation, Environmental; Esterases; Enzyme Stability; Bacterial Proteins; Burkholderiales
abstract: The biodegradation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and its derived intermediate breakdown products, represents a core focus of multidisciplinary research. While Ideonella sakaiensis PETase (IsPETase) and leaf-compost cutinase (LCC) efficiently depolymerize PET, many other PET-active hydrolases display stronger activity toward soluble PET intermediates such as bis- and mono(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET and MHET). Here, we describe a versatile carboxylesterase derived from Bacillus halotolerans (BhEstB). BhEstB is structurally related to BsEstB from B. subtilis but divergent from canonical PETases and most characterized MHETases, including IsMHETase, while clustering more closely with carboxylesterases such as TfCa. BhEstB displayed broad esterase activity toward pNP-esters, with maximum activity at pH 8 and 20-30 °C. Although it showed modest overall activity on the bulk polymer, BhEstB significantly outperformed the engineered variant LCCICCG and the recently published archaeal feruloyl esterase PET46 in turning over BHET and MHET. BhEstB exhibits remarkably high activity toward BHET and MHET, achieving complete conversion of 50 mM BHET within 1 h at 30 °C (kcat = 15.57 ± 1.25 s⁻1, Km = 6.54 ± 1.01 mM, corresponding to a catalytic efficiency of 2.38 × 103 M⁻1 s⁻1) and subsequent efficient turnover of 39.8 mM MHET (77% (± 0.7%)) into terephthalic acid (TPA) within 24 h. These results identify BhEstB as one of the most efficient BHET-hydrolyzing enzymes characterized to date. Collectively, these findings establish BhEstB as a versatile BHET/MHET active Bacillus carboxylesterase with modest activity toward commercial semi-crystalline PET powder, contributing to the expanding diversity of PET-intermediate-degrading enzymes. KEYPOINTS: • BhEstB exhibits structural divergence from canonical PET esterases. • BhEstB efficiently degrades significant amounts of BHET and MHET at 30 °C. • BhEstB demonstrates moderate activity on PET powder at elevated temperatures.

title: Environmental Aging Enhances Hydrodynamic Driven Microplastics Piezoelectric Catalytic Decomposition of Organic Pollutants.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are recognized as emerging environmental pollutants. However, their potential role in degrading pollutants under hydrodynamic conditions after environmental aging is frequently overlooked. In this study, three common MPs including polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polystyrene (PS) were investigated for their ability to enhance atrazine (ATZ) degradation after UV aging and under ultrasonic hydrodynamic treatment. Our findings demonstrate that environmental aging significantly boosts the piezoelectric catalytic activity of MPs, consequently accelerating pollutant degradation. UV-aged polypropylene (PP-8) exhibited the highest performance, achieving a piezoelectric catalytic degradation rate constant (k ═ 0.246 min-1), which is 22.36-fold higher than that of pristine PP (k ═ 0.011 min-1). Mechanistic studies revealed that polar carbonyl (C ═ O) functional groups formed during aging play a pivotal role for improving the piezoelectric properties of MPs. This enhancement promotes hydroxyl radicals (·OH) generation from water molecules, which drives pollutant degradation. Furthermore, this effect was found to be general as it was consistently observed in systems using MPs aged by different environmental processes (high temperature, mechanical wear, and Fenton oxidation) and exposed to various hydrodynamic conditions (oscillation and cavitation). This study provides new insights into the self-purification mechanisms of organic pollutants in natural environments.

title: Seasonality and maximum wind gusts correlate with microplastic concentrations in a freshwater stream system.
mesh: Microplastics; Environmental Monitoring; Rivers; Seasons; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Wind; Pennsylvania
abstract: We evaluate how meteorological and environmental variables relate to stream microplastic concentrations using regression-based models. Forty-nine water column samples were collected bimonthly over an annual cycle (September 2024-September 2025) from a stream in southeastern Pennsylvania, USA. Microplastic particles were isolated and quantified by light microscopy, and polymer types were characterized using scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Results from three separate multiple linear regression models (stepwise selection, LASSO, and elastic net) demonstrate high variability in microplastic counts, including pronounced seasonal variability (mean = 7.6 particles L⁻1, n = 49, 1σ = 4.9 particles L⁻1). All regression approaches identified colder temperatures and stronger wind gusts as important predictors of elevated microplastic concentrations. Repeated tenfold cross-validation indicated that models incorporating these variables explained approximately 80% of the variability in microplastic concentrations within this relatively small dataset (n = 49), highlighting their importance as the dominant environmental controls on microplastic abundance in Plum Run. When scaled by riparian area, the wind-sensitive component of the stream plastic flux is consistent with physically plausible atmospheric deposition rates. These results provide an indirect inference that environmental factors enhance transport of microplastics into waterways. Qualitative data from EDS and FTIR spectra indicate that polyester fibers comprise the majority of microplastic pollution in Plum Run. From this, we infer that increased laundering and shedding of synthetic clothing during winter may be a primary driver of higher pollution in winter months.

title: Microalgae-mediated aggregation facilitates the vertical transport of microplastics: the role of Cylindrotheca closterium under simulated conditions.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) released from aquaculture infrastructure represent a growing source of pollution in coastal environments, yet their fate in the presence of periphytic diatoms remains underexplored. This study investigates how the periphytic diatom Cylindrotheca closterium interacts with polyethylene (PE) MPs of two size classes (10-20 μm and 100-200 μm) under controlled laboratory conditions. Using 36-day time-series experiments, we examined cell attachment, aggregate formation, and sinking dynamics. C. closterium rapidly reached high biomass (>1.50 × 106 cells mL-1) and formed visible aggregates as early as day 11. Aggregation pathways differed by MP size: small particles became embedded within branched internal matrices, whereas large particles developed into dense, spherical flocs with external coatings of diatom cells. Large MPs served as nucleation cores, enabling higher MP incorporation per aggregate (mean 1.68-2.44 MPs) and generating attachment ratios exceeding 8.00 × 103 cells per particle in some treatments. Aggregate areas surpassed 1.7 × 105 μm2 in large-PE groups, and sinking velocities reached up to 3.70 mm s-1. Aggregate formation and downward transport occurred across all treatments, with distinct morphologies and performance depending on particle size and concentration. These results suggest that C. closterium promotes a robust pathway for MP aggregation and sedimentation through surface-mediated attachment rather than extensive extracellular matrix production. The size-dependent structural strategies highlight functional plasticity in capturing and retaining MPs. Overall, this study underscores the significant role of periphytic diatoms in regulating the environmental fate of aquaculture-derived MPs, providing new insight into biologically mediated removal processes in coastal ecosystems.

title: Effects of dry-wet alternation patterns on PFAS fate in sediments amended with microplastics.
abstract: The accumulation of PFASs in sediments is influenced by both dry-wet alternation (ADW) patterns and microplastic (MP) pollution, yet their combined effects on PFAS fate in water-sediment systems remain unclear. In this study, we investigated PFAS accumulation in sediments under three ADW patterns (1ADW, 2ADW, 3ADW) and continuous submergence (CS), combined with or without polypropylene (PP) MPs (1% w/w). The results showed that, relative to CS, ADW generally inhibited the accumulation of PFOA & substitutes, whereas its effect on PFOS & substitutes was pattern-dependent, with 3ADW even showing elevated accumulation. For individual compounds, HFPO-TA and PFHxS varied most across ADW treatments; Gen-X and PFBS least. MPs presence altered this trend: MPs promoted PFAS accumulation under ADW (with the highest increment of 44.68 μg/kg for PFOS & substitutes under 1ADW), but exhibited inhibition (for PFOA & substitutes) or weak (for PFOS & substitutes) effects under CS, indicating that the direction of MP-mediated regulation is highly dependent on hydrological conditions. Based on sediment physicochemical property differences and multiple linear regression (MLR) model results, compared to CS, ADW primarily inhibited PFAS accumulation by disrupting sediment flocculent structures and altering the role of DOM, whereas MPs presence enhanced PFAS retention by intensifying surface fragmentation, modulating key parameters (e.g., Zeta potential, BIX, and DOC), and serving as an additional sorption phase, thereby altering the original inhibition pattern imposed by ADW.

title: Precise identification and validation of microplastics using deep learning models in the Yellow River.
abstract: Investigating the spatial distribution and seasonal variations of riverine microplastics (MPs) is vital to aquatic ecological research. Mass suspended sediment within the Yellow River introduces severe background noise, which impedes conventional deep learning models from accurately extracting fine edge features of microplastics. Based on water samples collected from the Zhengzhou reach of the Yellow River, this study systematically evaluates a matrix of 24 hybrid encoder-decoder segmentation architectures covering six backbones (ResNet and ResNeXt series) and four decoders (FPN, DeepLabV3+, UNet, UNet++). The objective is to identify the optimal single model configuration (including network depth, topological layout, and feature fusion strategy) capable of accurately extracting fine edge features of microplastics under severe sediment interference.. Beyond standard segmentation metrics, three dedicated indices including Counting Error (CE), Background Complexity (BC) and 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95) are proposed to quantify the anti-noise robustness of each model. Grad-CAM visualization is adopted to interpret model spatial feature activation and target focus patterns, and micro-Fourier transform infrared (μ-FTIR) spectroscopy is utilized to cross-validate segmentation outputs. The ResNeXt-101 + UNet++ hybrid network delivers optimal performance. Equipped with grouped convolution and nested dense skip connections, this architecture bridges the information gap between shallow spatial details and deep semantic features, achieving a precision of 0.9534, a recall of 0.9991 and a mean absolute counting error (MAE) of 0.242. Microplastic abundances predicted by the model show excellent consistency with μ-FTIR measurements, addressing the common disconnection between image segmentation and spectroscopic identification in existing studies. This work develops an accurate intelligent pipeline for microplastic detection and quantification, facilitating routine surveillance and ecological risk assessment within the Yellow River Basin, while providing a methodological framework that warrants further validation in other sediment-laden aquatic environments.

title: Construction of Polydopamine@Crosslinked Polystyrene Core/Shell Polymeric Support for the Immobilization of Silver Nano-cluster: Adsorption and Selective Reduction of p-Chloronitrobenzene.
abstract: Polymers are promising catalyst supports because of their tunable composition and facile functionality. In this work, a core/shell polydopamine@crosslinked polystyrene support (XP-PDA) was first constructed, and silver nano-clusters were subsequently immobilized via in situ reduction to yield Ag@XP-PDA. Adsorption kinetic and temperature-dependent isotherm tests were conducted to compare the adsorption capacity of the catalysts toward the reactant p-chloronitrobenzene (P-CNB) and its corresponding hydrogenation product p-chloroaniline (P-CAN). At 298 K, Ag@XP-PDA reached adsorption equilibrium within 180 min, with distinct capacities of 38.5 mg g-1 for P-CNB, whereas only 9.2 mg g-1 for P-CAN. Increasing the temperature from 298 to 318 K enhanced the adsorption capacity for P-CNB (from 50.3 to 54.1 mg g-1) while suppressing that for P-CAN (from 15.3 to 11.6 mg g-1). This distinct temperature-dependent adsorption behavior indicates the chemisorption of P-CNB for substrate enrichment. Improved substrate adsorption and product desorption endow Ag@XP-PDA with over 90% P-CAN chemoselectivity at 318 K. Hence, the XP-PDA support enables both the stabilization of Ag nano-clusters and enrichment of the substrate, affording an efficient catalytic system for the selective reduction of P-CNB to P-CAN.

title: Tracing Industrial Microplastics Footprint in Fiji's Marine Environment.
mesh: Microplastics; Fiji; Environmental Monitoring; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Seawater
abstract: This study investigated the presence of microplastics (MP) in drainage channels that carry stormwater and greywater runoffs from areas surrounding the industrial sites on Viti Levu, Fiji's main island. Water samples were collected, digested with hydrogen peroxide, separated by density separation and filtered through an aluminum oxide Anodisc membrane filter (0.2 μm pore size) for particle recovery. The filter membranes were observed under a microscope for the presence, size and morphology of MP. 93.4% of particles ≥ 100 μm were confirmed as MP by ATR-FTIR. Across all sampling locations, an average MP concentration of 2.23 ± 0.78 MP L⁻¹ was observed, with the highest MP abundance (3.08 MP L- 1) at Site 5 and the lowest (1.26 MP L- 1) at Site 2. Fragments accounted for the largest number of MP (48.08%), followed by fibers (47.83%) and films (4.09%). Most of the MP (52.30%) were smaller than 500 μm. Polyethylene (PE, 46.29%) and polystyrene (PS, 33.76%) were the most prevalent polymers, reflecting their extensive use in packaging materials. These findings highlight the substantial role of industrial activities in MP contamination of the marine ecosystems. In Fiji, PS has been completely banned as a single use plastic, while PE is restricted under certain conditions. It is important to extend this ban to include PE and PS packaging materials to accelerate the elimination of these plastics from Fiji's environment.

title: Silver nanoparticles supported on DABCO-based ionic liquid-functionalized magnetic polystyrene for the efficient reduction of 4-nitrophenol.
abstract: The efficient conversion of nitrobenzene to aminophenols, typically achieved with metal catalysts or metal oxides, provides significant environmental benefits. In this study, a novel nanocatalyst was synthesized by immobilizing silver metal on DABCO-based ionic liquids supported on magnetic polystyrene. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized by XRD, TGA, EDS & EDS mapping, FT-IR, and ICP and subsequently evaluated as solid-phase catalysts for the reduction of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) with excess NaBH4 using UV-vis spectroscopy, which maintained good catalytic activity after six recycling cycles. The synthesized nanocatalyst was cost-effective and demonstrated excellent efficiency (⁓80% conversion) within 6 min, 15 mg of nanocatalyst, 25 mL of NaBH4 (2.5 mM), as well as straightforward separation during the reduction process. Additionally, kinetic analysis shows that the reduction of 4-NP follows a pseudo-first-order model with Kapp= 0.20 min- 1.

title: Hospital wastewater as a significant source of microplastics in Northern Iran: Abundance, polymer composition, and environmental risk assessment.
mesh: Microplastics; Iran; Wastewater; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Risk Assessment; Environmental Monitoring; Hospitals; Humans; Polymers
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous contaminants increasingly detected in aquatic environments and wastewater systems, raising concerns regarding ecosystem and human health. Hospital wastewater has been identified as a source of MPs entering municipal systems; however, data on their occurrence, characteristics, and associated risks remain limited. This study aimed to characterize MP contamination in hospital wastewater and assess the associated environmental and health risks. METHODS: Wastewater samples were collected from the influent and effluent of a hospital wastewater treatment plant in northern Iran. MPs were isolated using stainless-steel sieving followed by hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) digestion. Abundance, morphology, and size distribution were determined through microscopic examination, and chemical composition was analyzed using Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy Dispersive X-ray (SEM-EDX) and micro-Raman spectroscopy. The Pollution Load Index (PLI) and Hazard Index (HI) were calculated to evaluate contamination levels and associated risks. RESULTS: The analysis showed mean MP concentrations of 21.13 ± 12.8 particles L-1 in the influent and 1.45 ± 0.89 particles L-1 in the effluent, reflecting a removal efficiency of 93.13%. Morphologically, fibrous particles predominated (92-96%), with black as the most common color and sizes below 250 µm being the most prevalent. Identified polymer compositions included polyamide (PA), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyurethane (PU). Based on the calculated indices, the hospital wastewater reached a PLI of 1.86 and an HI of 1416.45, which corresponds to hazard level IV, primarily attributed to the high hazard score of PVC (5001) due to its carcinogenic monomer and additive leaching. CONCLUSIONS: Hospital wastewater is a significant source of MPs, particularly hazardous polymers such as PVC and PU. These findings highlight the need for targeted mitigation strategies, including advanced treatment processes and reduced use of toxic polymers in healthcare settings, to minimize MP discharge and protect environmental and public health.

title: Toxic cascade from oxidative stress to metabolic imbalance in Manila clams exposed to polyethylene terephthalate microplastics.
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most abundant plastic pollutants in marine environments. However, compared with other polymers, research on PET microplastics (MPs)-particularly their impact on benthic organisms in sediment environments-remains relatively scarce. In this study, we exposed Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum) to PET MPs in fragments and fibers of five sizes at concentrations of 0.8, 8, and 80 mg/kg dry weight (dw) of sediment for 21 days using a water-sediment exposure system. Mortality in Manila clams exposed to PET MPs remained unchanged, and each MP group accumulated in the digestive glands and gills. Chronic exposure to PET MPs increased reactive oxygen species production and SOD, IL-1β, and CASP8 levels in the gill and digestive gland tissues of clams. Integrated biomarker response analysis showed stronger correlations for fragments than for fibers, and for larger than smaller sizes, in both gill and digestive gland tissues. Furthermore, omics analysis confirmed a strong response in inflammation-related factors to fragment MPs, suggesting that PET MPs induce oxidative stress, inflammation, and cellular responses that lead to digestive and secretory dysfunction, which may cause morphological and metabolic changes in clams and ultimately adversely affect their health and survival. This study contributes to our understanding of the toxic mechanisms of PET MPs, focusing on their size and shape, and ultimately raises awareness of their harmful effects in the environment.

title: Using Weibull-derived λ-α parameters to diagnose physical processes controlling microplastic size dynamics in estuarine-coastal waters: A five-year study in Tianjin, Bohai Bay.
abstract: To elucidate the spatiotemporal evolution of microplastic particle size distributions and their controlling mechanisms in estuarine-coastal regions, this study conducted continuous monitoring in Tianjin coastal waters from 2021 to 2025. By coupling microplastic abundance and particle size analysis with Weibull distribution fitting to extract the rate parameter λ and shape parameter α, the impacts of sedimentation, fragmentation, and riverine input were investigated. The results showed a significant decline in both λ and α at all sites during 2021-2022, coinciding with extreme rainfall (978.4 mm) in Tianjin in 2021, indicating a pronounced riverine input pulse. After 2022, sites exhibited regional differentiation: northern nearshore sites showed sustained concurrent declines in λ and α (continuous input dominance); central sites exhibited stable low-level fluctuations (input-sedimentation balance); and certain sites displayed transient concurrent increases (episodic sedimentation dominance). Spatially, the multi-year mean λ increased with water depth, reflecting preferential settling of large particles. Notably, the concurrent decline in λ and α was accompanied by decreasing abundance at most sites, indicating that input particles became larger while total input flux decreased. This pattern may reflect the initial effectiveness of regional plastic control measures. This study demonstrates that the λ-α dual-parameter combination can effectively distinguish physical processes controlling microplastic size distributions, providing a new diagnostic tool for source identification and process attribution of microplastics in coastal waters.

title: Sustainable synthesis of a Zr-based UiO-66 MOF from PET waste for UV-assisted degradation of organic contaminants.
abstract: The coexistence of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste and persistent organic pollutants in aquatic environments requires comprehensive circular-economy strategies to valorize PET waste into functional materials for water treatment. In this study, post-consumer PET was converted to terephthalic acid (TPA) via a neutral hydrothermal depolymerization process and was used as an organic linker for the synthesis of a Zr-based UiO-66. The recovered linker and synthesized UiO-66 were characterized by FTIR, PXRD, TEM/SAED, nitrogen adsorption-desorption, UV-vis spectroscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and Mott-Schottky analysis. PXRD confirmed UiO-66 crystallinity, while TEM revealed nano-sized polyhedral particles with an average size of approximately 120 nm. The material exhibited a BET surface area of 822.2 m2 g-1, total pore volume of 0.379 cm3 g-1, and average pore diameter of 2.93 nm. Optical and electrochemical analyses showed a band gap of about 3.51 eV, n-type semiconducting behavior, and a flat-band potential of -0.68 V vs. Ag/AgCl. The photocatalytic activity of PET-derived UiO-66 was evaluated using methylene blue (MB) under UV light irradiation. Under optimized conditions, the catalyst achieved about 97.3% degradation with an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.024 min-1, which was about 12 times higher than that of direct photolysis. Radical scavengers' experiments showed that hydroxyl radicals (˙OH) acted as major reactive species, followed by superoxide radicals (˙O2 -) and photogenerated holes (h+). The catalyst showed good recyclability with about 86% activity retained after five cycles. These results offer an environmentally sustainable approach to recycle PET waste into a useful photocatalyst for water treatment.

title: Microplastics and toxic elements in small freshwater lakes and ponds in coastal Norway.
abstract: This study examined the occurrence of microplastics (MPs) and toxic elements in small freshwater lakes and ponds on islands in the Froan archipelago, Central Norway, evaluating marine plastic as a local contributor to environmental contamination. MP polymers and concentrations, along with toxic elements (As, Cd, Cu, Cr, Hg, Ni, Pb, Zn), were analyzed across freshwater, sediment, marine macroplastics, and adjacent soils across 12 waterbodies on seven islands, using Py-GC/MS (MPs) and ICP-MS (toxic elements). Polyethylene, polypropylene, and polystyrene were the predominant MP polymers, indicating secondary fragmentation. In freshwater, Cd and Zn reached Class V (very bad) status under Environmental Quality Standards, with concentrations up to 4.7 µg L⁻¹ and 260 µg L⁻¹, respectively. Marine macroplastics harbored extreme contaminant burdens from both legacy production additives and environmental adsorption, including Cd up to 415 µg g⁻¹ dw, Pb up to 800 µg g⁻¹ dw, Cr up to 186 µg g⁻¹ dw, and Zn up to 407 µg g⁻¹ dw. There were significant positive correlations for Zn concentrations in plastics, water, and sediments, alongside elevated element levels in shoreline soils (<0.3 m). This strongly indicates that plastic litter acts as a dynamic source and vector transferring toxic elements across compartments, accelerated by acidic conditions (pH < 7) triggering metal desorption. Notably, pollution levels differed greatly, even between ponds on the same island (e.g., a 270-fold difference in water Cd), highlighting the role of local topography on litter retention. These findings underline the role of marine plastic in amplifying contaminant burdens in coastal ecosystems.

title: Fabrication of gold nanostars for SERS detection of microplastics in water.
journal: Spectrochim Acta A Mol Biomol Spectrosc (2026)
abstract: Environmental contamination by microplastic particles has become a globally recognized issue, attracting increasing scientific and regulatory attention. In this study, a rapid and efficient method for detecting microplastics was developed using surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) combined with highly active substrates, enabling real-time monitoring and fast analysis. Gold nanostars (Au NSs) with sharp multi-branched structures were controllably synthesized using chloroauric acid (HAuCl₄), silver nitrate (AgNO₃), and ascorbic acid (AA). Their formation was achieved by regulating the anisotropic growth of gold via the underpotential deposition (UPD) of silver ions. The resulting Au NS colloid was then uniformly deposited onto a PVDF membrane through vacuum filtration, producing an Au NSs-PVDF substrate capable of both enriching and enhancing the SERS signal of microplastic particles. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations using a trimer model of Au NSs confirmed that the observed Raman signal enhancement originates from abundant electromagnetic "hot spots" generated by the sharp branches and the high specific surface area of the nanostars. SERS measurements demonstrated that rapid analysis of both single-component and binary mixtures of polystyrene (PS), polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyamide (PA) microplastics in aqueous environments can be completed within 10 min. Furthermore, the minimum detectable concentrations for single-component PET, PS, PE, and PA in lake water were 0.2 g·L-1, 0.4 g·L-1, 0.4 g·L-1, and 0.4 g·L-1 respectively, representing a significant improvement in detection efficiency.

title: Cellular toxicity and apoptosis-related responses to individual and combined exposure to microplastics and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) in Hediste diversicolor coelomocytes.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are emerging contaminants of increasing concern in marine ecosystems due to their widespread occurrence and ability to adsorb and transport hazardous chemicals such as perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS). PFOS is a persistent per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) with high environmental stability, bioaccumulative potential, and well-documented toxicity to aquatic organisms. However, the combined effects of MPs and PFOS on marine invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of environmentally relevant concentrations of MPs (50 mg kg-1 sediment) and PFOS (0.1, 0.5, and 1 μg kg-1 sediment) on the coelomic fluid of the benthic polychaete Hediste diversicolor after 7 days of sediment exposure. The MPs consisted of particles <30 μm composed of PVC, PET, PS, HDPE, LDPE, and PE with heterogeneous morphologies. PFOS accumulated in the coelomic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, with higher concentrations observed under co-exposure, suggesting that the presence of MPs may influence PFOS bioavailability and uptake. This increased accumulation was accompanied by pronounced cytotoxic and genotoxic effects, including lysosomal membrane destabilization, increased micronucleus frequency, and DNA fragmentation. Co-exposure also upregulated the pro-apoptotic genes p53, Bax, and Casp-3, while downregulating the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-2, indicating activation of apoptotic pathways. Overall, the effects of combined exposure varied according to the endpoint and PFOS concentration, with co-exposure producing greater responses for some endpoints but not consistently across all treatments. These findings highlight the increased hazard posed by the co-occurrence of MPs and PFOS and emphasize the need to consider contaminant mixtures in marine environmental risk assessment.

title: Synthesis of ultra-large Ti3C2T x MXene nanoflakes: enabling high-performance flexible transparent conductive coatings.
abstract: Flexible transparent conductive electrodes (FTCEs) are critical components in next-generation wearable electronics and display technologies. However, achieving low sheet resistance without compromising optical transparency remains a significant challenge due to percolation limitations in thin conductive films. MXenes, a rapidly expanding class of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal carbides and nitrides, offer remarkable potential as transparent conducting electrodes (TCEs) owing to their exceptional electrical conductivity, mechanical flexibility, and intrinsically hydrophilic nature. In this work, a modified orbital shaker-assisted Minimally Intensive Layer Delamination (Orbital-MILD) etching method is introduced, yielding ultra-large Ti3C2T x MXene nanoflakes with an average lateral size of ∼30 µm (optical-microscopy statistics over 168 individual flakes) and individual flakes reaching up to 48 µm - among the largest reported to date for solution-processed MXenes. The gentle orbital mixing action prevents flake fragmentation during both the etching and delamination stages, preserving the large lateral dimensions of the parent MAX phase particles. These large-flake inks were formulated into aqueous colloids and deposited onto flexible polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrates using slot-die coating - a scalable, alignment-promoting deposition technique. The resultant FTCEs demonstrated an electrical conductivity of 22 777 S cm-1 with a record figure of merit (FoMe) of 39, effectively eliminating the percolation bottleneck common in sparse nanomaterial networks. This work not only addresses a key limitation in MXene-based FTCE fabrication but also opens avenues for extending the method to other MXene systems, enabling scalable production of high-performance flexible electrodes.

title: Large Seasonal Variation in Microplastic Concentration from the Truckee River, United States.
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous in riverine environments worldwide, but arid river systems, characterized by large seasonal variations in discharge, remain understudied. Using a peristaltic pump, we collected samples for MP surface concentration analysis along the Truckee River in the western United States. Samples were collected using a 100 μm filter during fall 2022 and spring 2023 across 6 and 8 sites, respectively. The samples were analyzed with microscope-enabled Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy, and the resulting MP concentrations were compared to land use and river discharge. MP concentrations were higher in spring (mean 3.7 MP/L) than in fall (mean 0.4 MP/L), coinciding with an increase in river discharge. Statistical analyses revealed significant seasonal differences in polymer composition because of increased concentrations of poly-(ethylene terephthalate), polyethylene, and rubber in spring. These patterns likely reflect increased spring discharge mobilizing MPs from the surrounding landscape and riverbed sediments. These findings underscore the complexity of MP sources and transport and highlight the importance of seasonal sampling across discharge and land-use types. Additionally, polypropylene, poly-(ethylene terephthalate), and polyethylene were the dominant polymer types overall, demonstrating that reducing single-use plastic in the Truckee River Basin is important for protecting the river's water quality.

title: Airborne microplastics and associated heavy metal contamination in indoor and outdoor environments: Pollution levels and health risks in Metro Manila, Philippines.
mesh: Metals, Heavy; Philippines; Environmental Monitoring; Air Pollutants; Microplastics; Humans; Air Pollution, Indoor; Risk Assessment; Environmental Exposure
abstract: Airborne microplastics (MPs) have emerged as environmental pollutants that can co-occur with hazardous contaminants; however, evidence of heavy-metal associations with atmospheric MPs remains limited. This study investigated the abundance, characteristics, metal loadings, and health risks of airborne MPs in Metro Manila, Philippines. Air samples were collected from classroom, laboratory, dining room, office, living room, and store environments, followed by polymer identification via μFTIR and metal quantification using ICP-MS. MP concentrations ranged from 0.074 to 0.595 MP/m3 indoors (mean: 0.297 ± 0.20 MP/m3) and from 0.057 to 0.262 MP/m3 outdoors (mean: 0.173 ± 0.07 MP/m3), with no statistically significant difference. Fibers dominated the MP assemblage (52.38%), followed by fragments and films. PP, PET, and PE were the most prevalent polymers. Heavy metal concentrations ranged from 0.35 to 27521.66 mg/kg indoors and from 0.11 to 30556 mg/kg outdoors, with notable contributions from Zn, Cu, Ba, Pb, and Ag. These showed site-specific variations associated with room function and anthropogenic activity, with elevated Cu and Zn in high-activity indoor spaces. Pollution indices (PLI, MPI) indicated moderate pollution levels, while the ecological risk index indicated moderate ecological risk. Spearman analysis showed strong positive correlations between MPI-HM and As, Fe, and Zn (r = 0.70, p < 0.05), while PCA and HCA differentiated sampling sites by metal- and MP-related profiles. Inhalation risk assessment indicated low-to-moderate non-carcinogenic risk; however, the co-occurrence of toxic metals with respirable MPs highlights the occurrence of hazardous substances within the recovered airborne MP fraction. This study provides one of the first assessments of heavy metals associated with airborne MPs in indoor-outdoor urban environments.

title: Microplastic Contamination in Four Carnivorous Cultrinae Fish in Dianshan Lake, China.
mesh: Animals; China; Lakes; Microplastics; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Environmental Monitoring; Food Chain; Fishes
abstract: Microplastic (MPs) contamination in freshwater ecosystems threatens aquatic biodiversity. We investigated MPs ingestion in four sympatric Cultrinae fish species from Dianshan Lake, China, using gastrointestinal tract and stable isotope analyses. MPs were widespread, but abundance was low (1.25 ± 2.36 items/ind.). Fibers dominated and consisted mainly of polyethylene terephthalate and polyester, likely derived from fishing gear and domestic laundry. Cultrichthys erythropterus showed the broadest trophic niche and highest MPs diversity, suggesting that opportunistic feeding increases exposure to diverse polymers. MPs abundance was not related to trophic position (Cultrichthys erythropterus: P = 0.24; Culter dabryi: P = 0.07; Culter mongolicus: P = 0.09; Culter alburnus: P = 0.77), providing no evidence of biomagnification among the examined Cultrinae species. However, MPs abundance was negatively correlated with condition index in three species, but not in Culter alburnus. These findings suggest that trophic niche width may be more closely associated with MPs exposure than trophic position within the examined fish assemblage.

title: Biomonitoring microplastic pollution and polymer hazards using the Asian green mussel (Perna viridis): a baseline assessment from Santubong River, Sarawak, Malaysia.
mesh: Animals; Microplastics; Rivers; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Environmental Monitoring; Malaysia; Perna; Polymers
abstract: Microplastic contamination in aquatic organisms is a growing concern due to its ubiquity and potential toxicity. Currently, data on microplastic contamination and polymer hazards in green mussels (Perna viridis) from the Santubong River, Sarawak, is unavailable. In this study, green mussels from the Santubong estuary were analyzed, revealing a 100% occurrence rate and a mean abundance of 5.51 items/individual. Fibers (54.7%) and fragments (30.9%) were dominant, with transparent (40.9%), white (26.1%), and blue (23.8%) being the most prevalent colors. Most particles (83.6%) were < 1000 µm in size. Statistical analysis showed a moderate negative correlation (r = -0.40, p < 0.05) between microplastic abundance and soft tissue weight, suggesting potential impacts on the physiological condition of the mussels. Attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy identified polyamide (60%), polypropylene (23.3%), and polystyrene (10%) as the primary polymers. The prevalence of polyamide is linked to local aquaculture and fishing gear, such as nylon ropes. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) imaging confirmed extensive surface weathering, including cracks, pits, and fractures. The polymer hazard index (PHI) was calculated to be 3143.3, indicating a Level IV (high hazard) status. This study establishes a critical baseline for microplastic pollution management in P. viridis and environmental health assessments in Malaysian Borneo.
